transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brought me in is that some evenings after work, I just end up eating way, way more than I ever meant to. Especially if I've been really strict with myself all day. 

You know, I sell insurance, and most days I'm just glued to my desk, making calls. Just yesterday I had this client who kept me on the phone for an hour complaining about his auto premium going up, which, honestly, I have absolutely no control over. It's the underwriters! People just don't understand how the rates are calculated. 

But anyway, I get home after a day like that, and I'll have my regular dinner, but then it's like... I just keep going. I'll have bowls of cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers we have in the fridge, sweets, just all of it within a couple of hours. I usually buy those little crackers from the bakery down on 4th street, the one right next to the dry cleaners? They're so good, but my goodness, they've gotten expensive. Everything is so expensive lately, have you noticed? Going to the grocery store is just a shock every time now. 

But yeah, I just... I end up eating all of that stuff in one go, and it's been bothering me.
Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating a lot in one go?

Guilty? I'm... I'm not really sure if I'd call it guilt, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it using that word. It's funny you say guilt, though, because my mother used to talk about guilt all the time. She was very Catholic, you know? Everything was a sin. If you didn't scrub the baseboards before company came over, it was Catholic guilt time. 

I remember she used to make me use this specific lemon-scented cleaner for the floors, and to this day, I can't smell lemon without feeling like I'm supposed to be apologizing to someone. Which is a real shame, because I used to love lemon bars. My neighbor, Susan, she makes the absolute best lemon bars for our neighborhood block party every July. Well, she didn't do it last year because she was having her kitchen remodeled. They put in these gorgeous granite countertops, though I told her they require so much maintenance. You have to seal them every single year or they stain, and who has the time for that when you work full time? 

But... I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Something about how I feel?
Do you feel bad about yourself after these episodes of eating a lot in one go?

Bad about myself? I... I don't really know if I'd say I feel bad about myself, exactly. I haven't really noticed feeling like that, or I just haven't thought about it that way. 

My sister, Brenda, she always tells me I'm too hard on myself in general, but she's always been the confident one. She actually used to do pageants when we were in high school. Can you imagine? Just those local county pageants, but with the big hair and the heavy makeup. We used to go through so much Aqua Net hairspray. Do they even make Aqua Net anymore? I feel like everything is pump-spray now because of the ozone layer, which is a good thing, obviously. We have to protect the environment. 

We actually just looked into getting solar panels on our roof last month to do our part, but the installation guy they sent out was practically a kid, maybe twenty years old. He just didn't seem to know what he was talking about with the local grid regulations, and you have to be so careful with contractors these days. If they don't file the permits right, the city fines you, not them. 

But anyway... no, I'm just not sure I feel bad about myself after I eat. I don't really have an answer for that one.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these episodes?

Yeah, actually, I do. Once I get started on those nights, it's like I just keep going back to the kitchen even while I'm standing there telling myself to stop. I don't really feel back in charge of things until I'm just uncomfortably full. 

Speaking of the kitchen, we actually just had to get a new refrigerator last week because the ice maker on our old one completely gave out. It started making this awful grinding noise in the middle of the night, and I swear I thought someone was breaking in! My husband went downstairs with a golf club. Can you imagine? Just standing in the dark with a 9-iron ready to fight a kitchen appliance. We ended up having to buy a whole new unit because the repair guy said the parts for that model are discontinued. It's one of those French door ones now, which is nice, but the freezer is on the bottom. I just don't know if I like bending down that far just to get some frozen peas, you know? They look very modern, but practically speaking, I'm just not sold on the design. Do you have one of those bottom freezers?
Do you feel like you're eating much more quickly than usual during these episodes?

Eating quickly? I... I don't really know. I haven't really paid attention to how fast I'm eating, to be honest. I guess I'm just not sure. 

My husband, though, he eats like it's a race every single night. I tell him all the time, "Frank, the food isn't going to run away from you!" But he's been like that since we met. He says it's from growing up with three brothers, you had to eat fast or you didn't get seconds. His youngest brother, Tommy, actually just moved down to Florida. Fort Myers, I think. Or maybe it was Naples? Somewhere on the Gulf Coast. They bought this beautiful little condo right near the water, but I told him, I said, "Tommy, you have to think about the hurricanes." The insurance premiums down there are just through the roof right now. I see it all the time at work, people calling in completely shocked by their renewal rates. And with all the flooding they've had recently, a lot of the big carriers are just pulling out of the state entirely. It's a real mess for the homeowners. 

But, um... what was I saying? Did I answer your question?
Do you feel like you're in control of what or how much you're eating during these episodes?

Well, I think it's kind of like what I was just saying a minute ago about the kitchen. I really don't feel in charge at all. Once I start, I'll literally be telling myself to stop, but I just keep going until I'm uncomfortably full. I just lose all control. 

Which is strange for me, honestly, because normally I'm the one in control of everything. Especially at work. I sell insurance, mostly home and auto, and you have to be completely on top of the details there. Just this past Tuesday, I had a client, Mr. Henderson, trying to argue with me that he didn't need to list his sixteen-year-old son on his auto policy. I had to tell him, "Mr. Henderson, if that boy has a driver's license and lives under your roof, the underwriters are going to find out." 

People always think they can pull a fast one on the insurance companies, but they pull those CLUE reports and they see absolutely everything. If you had a roof leak five years ago, they know about it. Speaking of roofs, my next-door neighbor actually just got one of those metal roofs put on. It's supposed to last fifty years, which sounds like a great investment, but it is so incredibly loud when it rains. We had a thunderstorm roll through last night and it sounded like hail hitting a tin can right outside our bedroom window. I really don't know how they sleep through that racket. My husband Frank sleeps like a log, of course, but I wake up at every little noise. 

But, um, yes, to answer your question, I definitely don't feel in control when I'm eating like that.
Do these episodes of eating a lot usually happen when you're feeling stressed or upset about something?

I... I don't really know, to be honest. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. I guess I'm just not sure if I'm stressed or upset when it happens. 

Speaking of being upset, though, my sister called me yesterday just absolutely in tears. Her daughter, my niece Sarah, is getting married next spring, and the venue they booked just went bankrupt. Out of nowhere! They had already put down a huge deposit, and now the place is just shuttered. The owner apparently skipped town. I told my sister, "This is why you always need event insurance!" People never think they need it until something catastrophic happens. It's just like with weddings, you spend all this money on the flowers and the dress—oh, Sarah's dress is gorgeous, by the way, it has this beautiful lace detailing on the sleeves—but nobody thinks about protecting the actual investment of the day. 

I actually had a client last year who tried to file a claim on her homeowner's policy because her son's graduation party got rained out and the caterer still charged them. I had to explain that standard policies just don't cover a ruined potato salad because of a thunderstorm. People really don't read their policy documents. They just sign the bottom line and assume everything under the sun is covered. 

But, wait, what were we talking about? Was it about stress?
Do you think these episodes of eating a lot happen when you're feeling anxious or upset about something?

I think you might have just asked me something like that, didn't you? About being stressed or upset? I honestly still don't know. I really haven't noticed if anxiety has anything to do with it. I just don't have a good answer for you on that one. 

But you know, speaking of being anxious, people are just so incredibly anxious on the roads lately. I see it all the time with the auto claims we process. The accidents from just pure distracted driving and nerves are astronomical right now. Just the other day, I had a policyholder, Mrs. Gable, call in completely panicked because she rear-ended someone at a stoplight. She said she was too busy looking at her GPS. And honestly, those screens in the new cars are basically giant televisions right in the middle of the dashboard. How is anyone supposed to keep their eyes on the road? My husband Frank just bought a new truck, and the screen lights up the whole cabin at night. I tell him to dim it, but he says he can't figure out the menus. Everything is a touchscreen now. You can't even just turn a regular physical knob to get the air conditioning going anymore, you have to tap through three different screens. It is a massive safety hazard if you ask me. I always tell my clients they need to invest in dash cams, because it saves so much headache when it comes down to the adjusters trying to figure out who is at fault. 

But, oh gosh, I am rambling again. What did you ask me? Something about anxiety?
Do you ever feel guilty after one of these episodes of eating a lot in one go?

Guilty? Oh, um... I don't think so. I haven't really felt guilty afterwards, no. I mean, I feel uncomfortably full, like I said, but not guilty. 

You know who should feel guilty, though? The contractors who poured the driveway for our new neighbors across the street. They completely botched the slope, and now every time it rains, all the runoff pools right at the edge of their garage. I saw them out there with push brooms during that storm last night trying to sweep the water away from the foundation. I went over there a few weeks ago when they were just starting the build and I told the foreman, "You know, the grade here is really tricky, you need to make sure you're pitching that concrete at least a quarter inch per foot." But do they listen? Of course not. Nobody listens to a middle-aged woman giving construction advice. But I know a thing or two because my dad was a general contractor for thirty years. He built half the houses in our old neighborhood. He always said the foundation is the most important part of any job. If you get the foundation wrong, the whole house is going to settle unevenly, and then you've got cracked drywall and doors that won't close right. 

Actually, speaking of doors, I need to call the locksmith. The deadbolt on our back door is sticking again. Frank says he can fix it with some WD-40, but I told him that's just a temporary fix. You have to take the whole mechanism apart and actually clean it out. 

But, wait... did I answer your question? You were asking about feeling guilty, right?
Do you think these episodes of eating a lot are triggered by feeling overwhelmed or emotional?

I feel like you're asking me the same thing again... about being emotional or overwhelmed? I really, honestly don't know. I haven't noticed if being overwhelmed triggers it. I just don't have a clear answer for you on that. 

But you know, talk about being overwhelmed, you should see my inbox at work right now. It is absolutely overflowing. It's open enrollment season for the health insurance plans, and everyone waits until the absolute last minute to make their changes. And the questions they ask! People will email me asking if their specific brand of contact lens solution is covered under their flexible spending account. I tell them, "I sell the policies, I don't process the pharmacy receipts!" It's just constant. And the new software system the company rolled out last month is a complete disaster. It's supposed to streamline the application process, but half the time it crashes right when you're trying to upload a client's signature page. I spent two hours on the phone with IT on Tuesday, and the guy—he sounded like he was about twelve years old—told me to just clear my cache and restart my computer. As if I haven't tried that ten times already! 

Frank tells me I should just retire, take my pension and be done with it. He's been retired for two years now, and all he does is tinker in the garage and watch the Golf Channel. Which is fine, I guess, but I don't know what I'd do with myself all day. I need to be busy. I was thinking about taking up gardening, maybe putting in some raised beds in the backyard for tomatoes and peppers, but the soil back there is mostly clay. You have to amend it with so much compost just to get anything to grow. 

Anyway... I'm sorry, I lost track again. Did I answer your question about feeling emotional?
Do these episodes of eating a lot happen regularly, or is it something that happens every now and then?

Well, let me think about that. For the past few months, it's been happening most weeks, I'd say. Usually one or two nights a week where I just end up eating way, way more than I ever intended to. And then the next day, I feel like I have to make up for it, you know? So I'll skip meals or push myself to exercise a lot longer than usual. 

Speaking of exercising, the new treadmill Frank bought is an absolute monstrosity. It takes up half the guest bedroom. And it's one of those fancy ones with the screen built in where you can pretend you're running through the Swiss Alps or whatever. But the belt squeaks constantly. Squeak, squeak, squeak, every time your foot hits it. I told him he needs to lubricate the deck, but he insists it just needs to be "broken in." Broken in! It's a machine, not a pair of leather boots. I swear, the man can rebuild a carburetor blindfolded but he refuses to read the manual for a piece of exercise equipment. And don't even get me started on the delivery guys who brought it. They scuffed the paint in the hallway right by the baseboard, and when I pointed it out, they just shrugged and handed me the clipboard to sign. Customer service is just completely dead these days. It's like nobody takes pride in their work anymore. I see it all the time when I'm reviewing claims for water damage—plumbers doing shoddy pipe fittings, roofers cutting corners on the flashing... 

Oh, gosh, there I go again. I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. Did I answer your question about how often this happens?
Do these episodes of eating a lot cause problems in your daily life or affect your relationships with others?

Well, um, as far as problems in my daily life... I mean, I'm still keeping up with everything. I'm handling all my clients, and I'm still mentoring the new agents at the office. And the house is still running, you know? But I do sometimes feel a bit distracted. Like, if we have a company dinner or a public event, I get really self-conscious and less confident because I'm worried about how my clothes are fitting. 

Which, honestly, buying clothes lately has been a nightmare anyway. Have you been to the mall recently? It's like a ghost town. Half the stores are boarded up, and the ones that are open, the quality of the fabric is just terrible. Everything is that cheap polyester blend that pills after one wash. I bought a blouse for our annual sales conference—a really pretty emerald green, which is supposed to be my color—and I swear, one trip through the gentle cycle and the seam on the shoulder completely unraveled. I tried to take it back, but the girl at the register told me I had removed the tags so they couldn't process the return. I said to her, "How am I supposed to wash it with the tags still attached?" But she just stared at me blankly. It's that same lack of common sense I was talking about with the IT guy. Nobody knows how to problem-solve anymore. 

Like my nephew, Brian. He just graduated college with a degree in communications, whatever that means, and he can't even figure out how to change a flat tire. He called Frank last weekend stranded on the side of I-95 because he didn't know where the jack was in his own car. Frank had to drive forty minutes out there just to show him. I told Frank, "You're enabling him, he needs to learn the hard way," but Frank's a softie. 

Wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I got completely off track. Did I answer your question about it causing problems?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these episodes of eating a lot?

Well, weight changes... I haven't really noticed any significant changes, to be honest. My weight kind of just stays around the same, give or take a few pounds. I try not to step on the scale too often anyway, it just makes me crazy. 

But speaking of weight, Frank has been talking about putting on a few pounds since he retired. I keep telling him it's because he spends half the day sitting in his recliner watching golf. Have you ever tried to watch golf on television? It is the most mind-numbing thing in the world. Just whispering announcers and guys walking slowly across grass. I don't understand the appeal. But Frank loves it. He even bought this special orthopedic cushion for his chair because his lower back was acting up from sitting so much. I told him, "Frank, the cushion isn't going to fix the problem, you need to get up and move!" That's why he bought that awful squeaky treadmill, which, by the way, he has used exactly three times since it got delivered. 

And don't even get me started on the meals he expects now that he's home all day. When he was working at the plant, he'd just take a sandwich and a thermos of soup. Now he wants a hot lunch every day. Yesterday he asked me if I could make him a meatloaf for lunch. Meatloaf! In the middle of the day! I told him, "I am working from home, Frank, I am not your personal diner." I had three client calls scheduled back-to-back and a stack of policy renewals to review. I ended up just throwing a frozen pizza in the oven for him, which of course he complained about because the crust was too crispy. You really can't win sometimes. 

Oh, gosh... I'm rambling again, aren't I? I'm so sorry. What was it you asked me about? My weight? Did I answer that?
Do you think your episodes of eating a lot are ever triggered by feeling sad or depressed?

Well, triggered by feeling sad? I don't... I don't really think so. I mean, I'm not really a depressed person, you know? I get stressed, sure, but not really sad or down in the dumps like that. 

Though, speaking of sad, did you see the news about that local animal shelter closing down on the east side? It just breaks my heart. They lost their lease because the landlord sold the building to some developer who wants to put up another luxury condo complex. Just what this town needs, right? More overpriced apartments with gray laminate flooring and those awful Edison bulb light fixtures everywhere. It's so trendy right now, but it looks so industrial and cold. I went to an open house last weekend just to see what the market was doing—you know, keeping an eye on property values for insurance purposes—and the staging was just ridiculous. They had a single bowl of fake green apples on the kitchen island and not a single comfortable chair in the living room. Who lives like that? 

And the traffic over there is already a nightmare. If they add another two hundred units, you won't be able to get down Elm Street during rush hour at all. I was stuck there for twenty minutes just trying to turn left into the grocery store parking lot on Tuesday. And people are so rude! Nobody lets you in anymore. It used to be you'd wave, they'd flash their lights, you'd pull in. Now they just stare straight ahead and pretend they don't see your turn signal. It's that same self-centered attitude I was talking about. Everyone is just in their own little bubble. 

Oh, wait. I'm doing it again. I'm sorry, I really don't mean to keep drifting off like this. Did I answer your question about feeling sad?
Do you ever criticize yourself after one of these episodes of eating a lot?

Well, criticize myself... yeah, I guess I do. It's mostly about how my clothes fit, honestly. Like, if my waistband feels tight before a client luncheon or a leadership meeting, I start feeling like I look sloppy. I worry that people won't take me as seriously, even though I know I've still been doing my job perfectly well. 

But speaking of luncheons, they catered the last one from that new Italian place downtown, and I have to say, I was not impressed. They served this chicken piccata that was so salty you could barely eat it, and the capers were huge! I've never seen capers that size. I always buy the little nonpareil ones in the tiny glass jars. I tried to make chicken piccata for Frank last month, actually, because he said he wanted something "fancy" for a change instead of his usual pot roast. So I pounded the chicken breasts out thin, dredged them in flour, did the whole pan sauce with the lemon and the butter. And you know what he said? He said it was "too lemony." Too lemony! It's piccata, Frank, that is the entire point of the dish! 

I swear, his palate has completely regressed since he stopped working. If it doesn't come out of a slow cooker covered in brown gravy, he looks at it like it's alien food. I told my sister about it on the phone on Sunday, and she just laughed. But her husband is just as bad. He won't eat vegetables unless they're hidden in a casserole with a pound of cheddar cheese on top. It's like cooking for toddlers. 

Wait... I'm doing it again. I'm so sorry, I just get so wound up about Frank sometimes. What were we talking about? Did I answer your question about criticizing myself?
Do you think eating helps you feel better when you're stressed or upset?

Well, does it help me feel better? I don't... I don't really know if it does. I mean, I guess I've never really thought about it like that. When I'm stressed, I'm usually just trying to get through the day, you know? 

But speaking of being stressed, my sister called me in an absolute panic yesterday morning because her water heater completely flooded her basement. Just completely gave out. And of course, it happened on a Sunday, so she had to pay the weekend emergency rate for the plumber to come out. I keep telling her she needs to check her homeowner's policy because a lot of people don't realize that water backup isn't always covered under a standard policy, you have to add it as an endorsement. But does she listen to me? No. She just assumes because she pays her premium every month, everything is magically covered. 

I see it all the time at work. People come in furious because their roof leaked and ruined their drywall, and they find out their deductible is higher than the repair cost. It's like, people, you have to read the declaration page! It's not just a bunch of legal jargon, it's your actual coverage. I had this one client last week, Mr. Henderson—sweet older man, but completely clueless—who wanted to file a claim because a squirrel chewed through his patio furniture. A squirrel! I had to explain to him that rodents and vermin are specifically excluded. He was so upset, he threatened to take his business to State Farm. I just had to smile and nod, because what else can you do? 

Oh, goodness... I'm off on another tangent, aren't I? I am so sorry, my brain is just going in a million directions today. What was the question again? About feeling better when I'm stressed? Did I even answer that?
Do you think your eating episodes are ever triggered by feeling anxious or upset about something?

Anxious or upset? I don't... I don't really know. I guess I haven't really noticed a pattern like that with my eating. I mean, I get anxious about normal things, like making my quotas at work, but I wouldn't say it triggers anything. 

Actually, speaking of getting anxious at work, our regional manager came in on Thursday and completely changed the commission structure for life policies. Just out of nowhere! It is completely unfair to the agents who have been building their book of business for years. Brenda—she sits in the cubicle next to me—was practically in tears because she was counting on her quarterly bonus to pay for her daughter's wedding. The wedding is in October, and let me tell you, the prices for catering right now are just astronomical. They're doing a buffet, which I always think is a little tacky for an evening reception, but what can you do? I went to a buffet wedding last year and the carving station ran out of prime rib before our table was even called. We were table twelve, right by the kitchen swinging doors, which is the absolute worst place to sit because you hear the waitstaff banging plates and yelling all night. 

Anyway, Brenda is trying to figure out how to make up the difference, and I told her she needs to start cross-selling auto policies to her home clients, but she absolutely hates making cold calls. She says it feels too pushy. I told her, Brenda, we are in sales, pushy is in the job description! 

Oh, dear... I'm rambling again, aren't I? I always do this when I get going about the office drama. I'm so sorry. What did you ask me? Something about being anxious? Did that answer it?
Do you often think about what you've eaten after one of these episodes and wish you hadn't eaten so much?

Wish I hadn't eaten so much? I don't know... I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't really dwell on it, you know? Once it's done, it's done. 

But speaking of wishing you hadn't done something, Frank bought this ridiculous riding lawnmower off Craigslist last weekend. I told him, Frank, our yard is a quarter of an acre, you do not need a John Deere tractor to cut it! But he insisted he got a "great deal" on it. Well, the great deal broke down halfway through the front lawn on Tuesday. Just completely died, right there by the mailbox. So now we have this giant green monstrosity sitting in the grass, and the HOA sent us a letter about it yesterday. The HOA president is Susan Miller, and let me tell you, she has nothing better to do than patrol the neighborhood with a clipboard. Last month she cited the Jenkins family for leaving their trash cans out three hours past the deadline. Three hours! They had a new baby, for heaven's sake, you'd think she could show a little grace. 

And don't even get me started on the color she painted her front door. It's this bright, obnoxious teal. She claims it's "seafoam," but it looks like a melted crayon. If she's going to be so strict about everyone else's property, she should at least pick a tasteful color palette. 

Oh, wait... I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry, I just get so frustrated with Susan. What did you ask me? Something about wishing I hadn't eaten? Did I answer that?
Do you criticize yourself after eating a lot in one of these episodes?

Criticize myself? Um... I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I don't really sit around beating myself up about it. I just try to move on with my day. 

Although, moving on is exactly what my neighbor, Patty, needs to do. She has been complaining about the same pothole at the end of our street for three weeks now. Every single time I see her at the mailboxes, it's "Did you call the city? Have they fixed it yet?" I keep telling her, Patty, I work full time, I don't have time to sit on hold with public works! And honestly, it's not even that big of a pothole. You just have to steer a little to the left when you turn onto Elm Street. But she acts like it's a crater that's going to swallow her Buick whole. 

And speaking of her Buick, I have no idea how she even sees over the steering wheel to drive that thing. She's got to be barely five feet tall, and she refuses to use a booster cushion. I saw her back into the curb twice last Tuesday. Twice! I told Frank we need to park our cars in the driveway from now on because I do not trust her parallel parking. The last thing we need is a dented bumper right before we trade in the sedan. We're looking at getting one of those mid-size SUVs, maybe a Honda? Frank wants silver, but I think silver shows the dirt too much. 

Oh, my goodness, I am so sorry. I am just all over the place today, aren't I? My brain is just not cooperating. What were we talking about? Criticizing myself? Did I even answer you?

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Eating_Large_Amount
target_item.manifestation: What brought me in is that some evenings after work, especially when I've been strict all day, I end up eating way more than I meant to, like dinner, then cereal, crackers, leftovers, and sweets all within a couple hours.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S049).

patient.answer:
Hi. Well, I guess what brought me in is that some evenings after work, I just end up eating way, way more than I ever meant to. Especially if I've been really strict with myself all day. 

You know, I sell insurance, and most days I'm just glued to my desk, making calls. Just yesterday I had this client who kept me on the phone for an hour complaining about his auto premium going up, which, honestly, I have absolutely no control over. It's the underwriters! People just don't understand how the rates are calculated. 

But anyway, I get home after a day like that, and I'll have my regular dinner, but then it's like... I just keep going. I'll have bowls of cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers we have in the fridge, sweets, just all of it within a couple of hours. I usually buy those little crackers from the bakery down on 4th street, the one right next to the dry cleaners? They're so good, but my goodness, they've gotten expensive. Everything is so expensive lately, have you noticed? Going to the grocery store is just a shock every time now. 

But yeah, I just... I end up eating all of that stuff in one go, and it's been bothering me.

inference.note: Added potential eating disorders due to patient's description of binge eating episodes

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences guilt after binge eating
doctor.question: Do you usually feel guilty after these episodes of eating a lot in one go?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt after the eating episodes. While the profile covers the eating episodes, loss of control, and compensatory behaviors, it does not explicitly mention feelings of guilt after bingeing.

patient.answer:
Guilty? I'm... I'm not really sure if I'd call it guilt, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it using that word. It's funny you say guilt, though, because my mother used to talk about guilt all the time. She was very Catholic, you know? Everything was a sin. If you didn't scrub the baseboards before company came over, it was Catholic guilt time. 

I remember she used to make me use this specific lemon-scented cleaner for the floors, and to this day, I can't smell lemon without feeling like I'm supposed to be apologizing to someone. Which is a real shame, because I used to love lemon bars. My neighbor, Susan, she makes the absolute best lemon bars for our neighborhood block party every July. Well, she didn't do it last year because she was having her kitchen remodeled. They put in these gorgeous granite countertops, though I told her they require so much maintenance. You have to seal them every single year or they stain, and who has the time for that when you work full time? 

But... I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Something about how I feel?

The last thing we need is a dented bumper right before we trade in the sedan. We're looking at getting one of those mid-size SUVs, maybe a Honda? Frank wants silver, but I think silver shows the dirt too much. 

Oh, my goodness, I am so sorry. I am just all over the place today, aren't I? My brain is just not cooperating. What were we talking about? Criticizing myself? Did I even answer you?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits recurring episodes of eating significantly more food in a short period than most people would eat under similar circumstances, with episodes marked by rapid eating and a sense of lack of control. The patient reports feeling uncomfortably full afterward and sometimes criticizes herself about her eating, but does not consistently report feelings of guilt or depression following these episodes.
